definition: The set of GPUs that can reach each other directly over NVLink, without going through a network card. Inside it GPUs read and write each other's memory at NVLink speed; outside it traffic falls back to the much slower scale-out network.

NVIDIA's rack-scale system in which 72 GPU packages share one NVLink domain through 18 (Blackwell) or 36 (Vera Rubin) NVLink switch chips. The number counts GPU packages; NVIDIA briefly counted dies ('NVL144') before reverting in 2026.
A 1U tray in an NVL72 rack that holds NVLink switch chips (two per tray in GB200 NVL72), a management controller and rear connectors that plug into the copper spine. Nine trays switch all 72 GPUs.
The bundle of copper twin-axial cables at the back of an NVL72 rack that joins every GPU tray to every switch tray. NVIDIA describes about 5,000 cables totalling about two miles in GB200 NVL72.

A connector that mates automatically when a tray slides into the rack, without anyone plugging cables by hand. NVL72 trays use them to join the NVLink spine, which makes trays swappable and cabling errors rarer.

Four-level pulse-amplitude modulation: each symbol on the wire carries two bits instead of one, doubling the data rate at the same symbol rate. NVLink moved to PAM4 with Hopper; it is more sensitive to noise, which shortens copper reach.
A passive copper cable with connectors on both ends and no electronics inside. It uses almost no power and rarely fails, but at 200 Gb/s per lane a passive cable reaches only about a metre.

Energy needed to move one bit across a link; watts divided by bits per second. A DSP-based optical module uses about 15-19 pJ/bit, co-packaged optics about 5 pJ/bit and a passive copper cable adds almost nothing beyond the chips' own SerDes.

A large printed-circuit board in the middle of a rack or chassis into which compute and switch blades plug from both sides, replacing cables. NVIDIA's Kyber rack uses a midplane instead of the NVL72's cable spine.
NVIDIA's next rack design for Rubin Ultra: 144 GPU packages on vertical blades joined through a printed-circuit midplane, at roughly 600 kW. NVIDIA targets H2 2027; a slip to 2028 has been reported.
The internal name for the rack design used by GB200, GB300 and Vera Rubin NVL72: horizontal compute and switch trays joined by a rear copper NVLink spine.

The two communication steps of every mixture-of-experts layer: dispatch sends each token's activation to the GPUs holding its chosen experts; combine sends the expert outputs back to be summed. Together they form an all-to-all exchange.

Spreading a mixture-of-experts model's experts across many GPUs (for example 64-144) so each GPU holds only a few. It frees memory for larger batches and caches, but makes dispatch and combine traffic cross more GPUs.
An open standard for connecting chiplets inside one package. Reports suggest third-party chips could attach an NVLink chiplet over UCIe under NVLink Fusion.
NVIDIA's modular reference architecture for servers and racks, which partners use to build systems around NVIDIA or partner chips. AWS plans to place Trainium4 in MGX racks with NVLink.
A small service processor on a server or switch tray that monitors health, power and firmware over a separate management network, even when the main chips are off.
